This is a list of the candidates of the 2026 Victorian state election.

Retiring MPs

[edit]

The following members announced that they will not be contesting the 2026 election:

Labor

[edit]
  • Jackson Taylor MLA (Bayswater) – announced 23 September 2025[1]
  • Steve McGhie MLA (Melton) – announced 23 September 2025[1]
  • Emma Vulin MLA (Pakenham) – announced 30 September 2025[2]
  • Jordan Crugnale MLA (Bass) – announced 2 October 2025[3]
  • Natalie Hutchins MLA (Sydenham) – announced 16 October 2025[4]
  • Shaun Leane MLC (North-Eastern Metropolitan Region) – announced 1 December 2025[5]
  • Danny Pearson MLA (Essendon) – announced 10 April 2026[6]
  • Mary-Anne Thomas MLA (Macedon) – announced 10 April 2026[6]
  • Gayle Tierney MLC (Western Victoria Region) – announced 10 April 2026[6]
  • Lily D'Ambrosio MLA (Mill Park) – announced 30 July 2026[7]
  • Harriet Shing MLC (Eastern Victoria Region) – announced 30 July 2026[7]
  • Jacinta Allan, MLA (Bendigo East) – announced 14 August 2026[8]
  • Maree Edwards MLA (Bendigo West) – announced 27 August 2026[9]
  • Sonja Terpstra MLC (North-Eastern Metropolitan Region) – announced 12 October 2026[10]

Liberal

[edit]
  • Bill Tilley MLA (Benambra) – announced 13 March 2024[11]
  • David Hodgett MLA (Croydon) – announced 6 August 2025[12]
  • Michael O'Brien MLA (Malvern) – announced 9 September 2025[13]
  • Kim Wells MLA (Rowville) – announced 14 September 2025[14]
  • Wendy Lovell MLC (Northern Victoria Region) – announced 5 January 2026[15]
  • Joe McCracken MLC (Western Victoria Region) – announced 12 January 2026[16]

National

[edit]
  • Peter Walsh MLA (Murray Plains) – announced 26 November 2024[17]
  • Tim Bull MLA (Gippsland East) – announced 19 May 2026[18]
  • Kim O'Keeffe MLA (Shepparton) – announced 21 July 2026[19]

Greens

[edit]
  • Tim Read † MLA (Brunswick) – announced 29 January 2026 (died 19 September 2026)[20]

Legalise Cannabis

[edit]
  • David Ettershank MLC (Western Metropolitan Region) – announced 2 June 2026[21]

Resignations and disendorsements

[edit]
DatePartyCandidateSeatDetails
December 2025 Liberal Andrew Kilmartin Ripon Withdrew due to Huntington's disease diagnosis[470][471]
3 January 2026 Family First Bernie Finn Western Metropolitan Withdrew due to disagreements with party leadership[472][473]
29 January 2026 Greens Tim Read Brunswick Withdrew due to metastatic cancer diagnosis[313][474]
20 March 2026 Liberal Dinesh Gourisetty Western Metropolitan Withdrew due to controversy over providing a character reference for a child sex offender[475]
16 July 2026 Socialist Owen Cosgriff Bendigo East Withdrew due to a family illness[476]
17 July 2026 Liberal Moira Deeming Western Metropolitan Disendorsed after making unsubstantiated claims of assault against fellow MP Matthew Guy.[477] Ran as a Family First candidate.
25 August 2026 Labor Indah Johannes Evelyn Withdrew due to Hodgkin lymphoma diagnosis[150]
1 October 2026 One Nation Greg Hansford Eastern Victoria Withdrew due to health issues[478]
12 October 2026 Liberal Grant Hutchinson Croydon Disendorsed due to a legal dispute between the candidate and his law firm[120]
31 October 2026 One Nation Matthew Collins Melbourne Withdrew over controversial social media posts[479]
